chapter: Building McShann's big band and blues records
title: Parker's arrangement 'What Price Love' and the Dallas Decca session
summary: Ramey remembers only one Parker arrangement, recorded in Dallas, which Decca rejected for blues.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I think Jay told me once that Parker wrote some arrangements.

Well, I only remember one that he wrote. Most of the things we did was in his heads, but he wrote that thing, "What Price Love?", which he recorded in his own name as "Yardbird Suite" (PHONETIC). And we recorded that on our first recording we did with Decca. But we never heard any more of it.
We recorded that in Dallas with --
I wonder what -- let me make a note of that. I don't think -- I think they must have destroyed it.

Well, we recorded it, and they played it back for us and everything. But they said, no, this is a little far away from the picture we have of Jay McShann. We want some blues. So -- in fact, McShann -- we stayed in that studio and played it lots of things for them and they listened and told us to go back to the blues. In fact, if you notice, lots of things, you could probably tell that they were being made up right there (inaudible). Brown had the words as we went along.
